messages.author: 9ebae4f0ba958a1e
messages.subject: help with strange results
parts:
Hi all,

I am beginner user of Distance.

We have a project in Brazilian Amazon Forest, in Terra do Meio, Pará State. There are 9 tracks of 5km each. After 2 years of data collecting, we still have few observations for most species, but the monitoring will keep going. 

For some species with enough observations (n=+40), the  Distance analyses is getting results like this: “0.28440E+06” or “0.18999E+06”, for density and abundance.

I do not understand and I am confused to interpret this kind of results.

Am I doing something wrong? Anyone can help me?

Let me know if you need more information.

Thanks a lot.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] help with strange results
parts:
Victor

Glad you spotted something not quite right.  I suspect the problem has to do with incorrectly specifying the units in which transects, perpendicular distances and areas were measured.  If you are doing your analysis in R, you will need to carefully read the section in the ds() function regarding the "convert.units" argument.  If you are using the programme Distance, be sure you have correctly entered information on this page of the project wizard:

If you need more help, let me know.
